summary: Creates staggered time-offset phase interpolation on POP attributes, similar to Phaser CHOP. Each point can output a Phase/Phaser-style value that moves from 0 to 1 over a cycle at different offsets.

key_params.note: Input attribute scope that drives phase staggering

key_params.note: Automatic, float, or int output casting

key_concepts: Phaser POP performs staggered time-offset interpolation on a POP attribute, similar to Phaser CHOP.
Each point can output a Phaser/Phase-style value that rises from 0 to 1 over a cycle at different offsets.
Phase Attribute Scope controls the input staggering source; multi-component phase attributes produce multi-component phase output.
Fraction drives the phase cycle and can be smoothed, reversed, reranged, cast, and written to a chosen output attribute scope.
The output phase is intended as a downstream mask or blend driver for animation, not as automatic deformation of every target attribute.
Output attribute metadata controls type, component count, default value, and class when automatic inference is not enough.
common_gotchas: Phase can be multi-component when the phase attribute scope is multi-component.
Extend behavior above 1 can clamp, cycle, mirror, mirror-slope, or add; choose deliberately for looping animations.
Use the output phase as a downstream blend/mask driver rather than expecting Phaser POP to animate every target directly.
